annotation.title_clean: Safety Design of Personal Care Robots Based on Safety Standard Considering Characteristics of Children
annotation.title_en: Safety Design of Personal Care Robots Based on Safety Standard Considering Characteristics of Children
annotation.venue: Proceedings of the 2020 JSME Conference on Robotics and Mechatronics (Robomech), Kanazawa
annotation.summary_en: Japanese conference paper analysing how Japanese safety standards for personal care robots (JIS B 8445, JIS Z 8050, toy safety ST standards) address children, identifying gaps, and proposing a simple collision-safety evaluation using a dummy robot and cushioning materials to measure impact force and impulse.
key_provisions_or_claims: Personal care robot safety standards require consideration of children but give no specific methods.
Authors build a correspondence table combining JIS safety standards with child-specific standards for risk assessment.
Gaps identified in existing standards for children's active contact with robots.
Dummy-robot collision experiments tested six cushioning materials for impact force and impulse.
Normalising by collision speed reduced variance for some cushioning materials.
